story.title: Almost No One in the Camp
story.text: Cao Cao's army reached the Han River, and almost no one was left in Zhao Yun's camp.
story.narration: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, Cao Cao came in person to fight for Hanzhong. Most of Zhao Yun's soldiers were out fetching grain, and only a small guard was left in the camp. Cao Cao's army pressed up to the walls, and everyone inside held their breath — to bar the gate, to fight, or to run, there was no time for any of it.

story.title: He Opened the Gate Wide
story.text: He opened the gate wide, laid the flags down, and Cao Cao's men withdrew.
story.narration: Zhao Yun did not bar the gate and hold it. He had the gate thrown wide open, the flags laid down, and not a drum beaten — the camp was as quiet as if no one were there. Cao Cao's men watched from the gate for a while, and the longer they watched, the more certain they grew that someone was waiting inside; in the end they did not dare come in, and withdrew. This is recorded in the Yun Bielu, the supplementary life of Zhao Yun.

keyMoment.question: Cao Cao's army is just outside the gate, and the camp is almost empty. What do you do?

options.text: Hold still — open the gate wide and let him doubt
Bar the gate at once and hide everyone
options.hint: A barred gate tells him the camp is afraid.

options.text: Shout from the wall, so he thinks you have many men
options.hint: The louder you shout, the longer he stops to look.

keyMoment.reveal: The more tense it gets, the less you may move — the quieter it looks, the less sure he is.

misconceptions: Holding still means there is nothing to do but wait to be beaten
When you are few, you should hide where he cannot see you

quiz.question: How did Zhao Yun keep Cao Cao's army from entering the camp?
options: He opened the gate wide and laid the flags down, so the camp looked empty
He barred the gate and ran out the back
He shouted from the wall to look like a crowd
quiz.explanation: The quieter it was, the less sure he felt — what he feared was not numbers, but not knowing.

quiz.question: Before you go on stage your hands are shaking and the audience keeps watching you. What is better?
options: Stand still, take one slow breath, then begin
Start at once and talk fast to cover it
Look down at the floor and wait for someone else to speak
quiz.explanation: The more tense it gets, the less you may move — steady yourself first, and no one can see that you are nervous.

levelScript.doubtLine: He glances at the gate again...
